mechanism_narrative: Persistent depression in TRANSIT mobility (-52 to -55% across all four weeks) indicates sustained lockdown conditions that directly suppress retail foot traffic. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed over the next four weeks because the underlying transit constraint persists.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT averaged -53.6% over last 4 weeks with no recovery trend
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 15 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (14.3 to 15.9% above baseline) combined with severely depressed RETAIL_REC (-56 to -60%) indicates substitution of home-based activities for retail consumption. If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, this behavioral shift will sustain low RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 14% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL consistently 14-16% while RETAIL_REC is -56 to -60%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below 10% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -40%, indicating behavioral reversion to pre-lockdown patterns.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -46 to -48% over four weeks with no deterioration trend. If workplace restrictions remain constant (not tightening), retail mobility will begin recovery within two weeks as workers establish new commuting routines that include retail stops.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change is less than 2 percentage points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES variance across 4 weeks is only 1.5 percentage points
failure_condition: WORKPLACES drops below -50% in any week over the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase by at least 5 percentage points from current baseline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high volatility (-29 to -46% across weeks), suggesting weather-driven or policy-driven fluctuations in outdoor activity. When PARKS mobility rises above -30%, retail-adjacent outdoor recreation increases, pulling RETAIL_REC upward within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -30% from prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS ranged from -29% to -46%, showing 17-point swing
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -30% in any week but RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 3 percentage points in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable at -23 to -27% across four weeks, indicating essential shopping is maintained at a floor level. This stability signals that consumer purchasing power and necessity-driven mobility remain intact, creating a foundation for discretionary retail recovery if restrictions ease.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within -20% to -30% band for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM variance is only 4 percentage points across 4 weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM drops below -35% or rises above -15%, indicating either severe demand destruction or policy change that would confound the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between TRANSIT collapse (-54%) and WORKPLACES depression (-47%) creates a dual-constraint regime where both commuting and retail access are blocked. Recovery in RETAIL_REC requires simultaneous improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES; if only one improves, retail remains suppressed.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT -54.4% and WORKPLACES -47.0% in most recent week
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above -40% while the other remains below -50%, or RETAIL_REC rises above -45% despite both proxies staying below -45%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown no improvement trend over four weeks (ranging -56 to -60%), indicating policy restrictions are binding and unchanged. Absent a policy shift signal (observable as TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovery), RETAIL_REC will remain at current depressed levels over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC four-week mean is below -55% AND TRANSIT four-week mean is below -50%
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC mean over 4 weeks is -58.4%, TRANSIT mean is -53.6%
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -40% in any week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds -50%.

If PARKS mobility continues to fluctuate above -35%, outdoor retail (markets, street vendors) will capture some diverted demand, producing a modest net increase in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
